Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving fast on a dedicated deployment for two production endpoints and need a realistic sizing proposal to take to procurement. High-level requirements below — happy to jump on a call but wanted something written we can circulate internally.

- Models: 70B decoder-only (approx. 32k context) for assistant flows, and a smaller 13B variant for low-latency tasks.
- Traffic profile (expected steady -> peak): 15 qps steady, 120 qps peak (short bursts) across both endpoints; average request ~1.2k tokens in / out.
- Latency SLO: p95 generation < 700ms for assistant flow (70B).
- Compliance: VPC + customer-managed KMS.
- Timeline: production by end of Q2; want a POC for one month first.

Specific asks:
1) Rough GPU counts and suggested instance types for the dedicated pool.
2) Impact of KV cache for 32k context on per-GPU memory and how that changes with quantization strategies (q4/nf4/int8).
3) If you can show a conservative & aggressive plan (headroom / autoscale), that would be ideal.

I've attached our internal usage spreadsheet for reference.

Best,

From: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.example.com, aditya_rao@redwood.example.com, laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Sizing request: Arcadia — draft calc (internal)

Folks — forwarding Sophie's ask. Key inputs: 70B with 32k context is driver. They estimate peak 120 qps bursts. Need a short write-up we can send Sophie with conservative and recommended options + POC ask.

I sketched some quick back-of-envelope numbers below. Please critique and fill gaps. We'll include the spreadsheet and a slide with the final counts.

--- BEGIN B-O-E ---
Assumptions & terminology:
- Target model: 70B decoder, FP16 weight baseline. For raw weight storage in FP16: ~70B * 2 bytes ≈ 140 GB (not accounting for optimizer state which we don't need at inference). Storage is distributed across GPUs.
- Quantized weight sizes (typical): q4 ~ 4 bits per param (~35 GB equivalent), int8 ~ 8 bits (~70 GB). Effective in-memory working set also includes embeddings/indexes and shard overhead (~+10%).
- KV cache: large driver for 32k context. Empirical measurement (70B arch similar to what we validated): ~0.75 bytes per token per layer pair * num_layers -> ballpark: 0.6–0.9 GB per 1k tokens for 70B when fully materialized (readout + key/value). For 32k ~ 20–30 GB of KV per concurrent sequence.
- Concurrency assumptions: bursty traffic may have many concurrent active sessions each keeping KV in memory. If average in-flight concurrent sequences at peak = 250 (this is derived from 120 qps * average generation time), KV totals scale linearly. We recommend isolating long-session traffic (assistant flows) behind a smaller pool with larger memory per-GPU and short queries on a separate pool.

Initial sizing sketches: (H100-80GB baseline)
Option A — Conservative (FP16, prioritize fidelity):
- Model weights: need ~140GB => 3-way sharded across 6 x 80GB GPUs (weights + shard overhead + temp) per replica.
- KV cache: 32k per sequence ~25 GB. If we allow 2 sequences resident per GPU (for throughput), need ~50 GB extra — i.e., offload or increase replica count.
- Suggested pool: 16 x H100-80GB across 2 replicas (8 GPUs per replica) to meet p95 targets with headroom for bursts and autoscale.
- Notes: high quality, higher cost, meets latency if batching optimized.

Option B — Recommended (q4 quant + KV optimization):
- Quantize weights to q4_f4: effective model weight storage ~35–40 GB. Shard across 4 GPUs (plus overhead) — fits comfortably on 80GB instance with room for KV.
- KV cache: with memory left for KV we can accommodate ~2 concurrent 32k sequences per GPU (or more sequences with KV prefix sharing).
- Suggested pool: 12 x H100-80GB across 3 replicas (4 GPUs per replica) with intelligent KV cache eviction and prefix sharing to keep p95 < 700ms.
- Expected tradeoffs: minimal quality delta for most assistant workloads; substantial cost savings vs FP16.

Option C — Aggressive cost-saver (int8 + cold offload):
- Use int8 quant where model supports it reliably -> weights ~70 GB total. Use NVMe/KV offload for very long contexts; pipeline cross-GPU for slower p95 but lower GPU count.
- Suggested pool: 10 x H100 with aggressive autoscale + fallback to smaller 13B model for latency-critical paths.

Operational suggestions:
- Split traffic: long-session assistant (32k) on small high-memory pool; short queries on scaled lower-memory pool.
- Start POC in q4 quant mode to validate quality; keep FP16 as fallback.
- Autoscale policy: keep base reserved pool = 60–70% of expected steady throughput and allow rapid burst nodes + prewarmed replicas for 70B.

Open questions for sizing accuracy:
- Can Sophie share the distribution of tokens-per-request (percentiles) and expected concurrency for long sessions?
- Do they expect session affinity (same user keeps KV in memory) vs stateless requests?

--- END B-O-E ---

Pls review and I'll tidy into a one-page summary for Sophie. Marcus — can you sanity-check the KV per-token numbers vs our latest perf tests? Aditya — I'll need a quick cost delta for q4 vs fp16 to include.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: marcus_lin@redwood.example.com

Subject: Re: FW: Sizing request: Arcadia — draft calc (internal)

Thanks Marissa — quick sanity checks & adjustments from perf lab:

- KV numbers: our lab tests on a 70B-like architecture show KV ~0.72 GB per 1k tokens (end-to-end hot KV memory including layer packing). That means 32k context ~23 GB per active sequence (within Marissa's 20–30 GB ballpark).
- Weight storage: q4_f4 encoding plus tensor packing and compression gives ~38–42 GB equivalent with library overhead; plan for +15% shard overhead. So a 4-way shard on 80GB H100 is comfortable and leaves ~10–18 GB for KV per GPU.
- Concurrency math: if we size for 120 qps bursts with average generation latency ~400ms in q4 config -> concurrent generation workers ~48 (120 * 0.4). But for long sessions avg generation may be higher; use safety factor 3 -> ~144 concurrent active sequences. At 23 GB per sequence that is infeasible to keep all KV resident. Hence the split-pool recommendation is mandatory.

Refined recommendations:
- POC (30 days): 8 x H100-80GB in q4 mode dedicated to Arcadia assistant traffic with 2 prewarmed replicas (total 12 GPUs available for burst). This lets us validate quality and measure real concurrency.
- Production conservative: 18 x H100 across two replica groups (9+9) in q4 with autoscale up to 24 for sustained higher loads between 2–6 weeks.
- Fallback path: maintain a small FP16 pool (4–6 GPUs) to serve heavy long-session users if quality regression is observed.

I'll add actual perf numbers from the lab runs into the slide and generate cost comparisons for q4 vs fp16 for Aditya.

—Marcus
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Arcadia Dedicated Sizing — proposal & next steps

Hi Sophie,

Thanks — attached is a short one-pager and our recommended sizing proposal based on the inputs you shared and our lab validation. Summary (TL;DR):

- POC (30 days): 8 H100-80GB dedicated in q4 quant config + 4 GPUs prewarmed for burst (total 12 GPUs available to Arcadia). Objective: validate quality & measure real concurrent long-session behavior.
- Production target (recommended): 18 H100-80GB across 2 replica groups (9 + 9) with autoscale up to 24 GPUs for sustained peak bursts. This balances latency SLOs and cost.
- Cost/quality: q4 quantization reduces GPU footprint by ~35–45% vs FP16 for the 70B model; we included a cost tab in the attached spreadsheet for q4 vs fp16 and an FP16 fallback plan.
- Operational: split long-session traffic to a high-memory pool, short queries to a separate scaled pool; enable prefix/KV sharing and eviction for long tails.

Next steps we propose:
1) Kick off a 30-day POC in q4 mode (we can provision the pool as early as next week).
2) Share token-percentile distribution and any expected session-affinity patterns.
3) Contract note: reserved baseline for POC + optional burst credits; Laura will follow up on procurement language.

Available times for a 30-min sync this week: Mon 11–1pm PT, Wed 9–11am PT.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

(attachments: Arcadia_Dedicated_Sizing_v1.pdf, cost_estimate_q4_vs_fp16.xlsx)
